status.note: Not recorded: whether and how the university operates for foreign students in 2026–27 is unresolved (adversarial re-check, 2026-10-12). Leads: an official 2022 rector interview says teaching resumed on 1 April 2022 in remote format, deans and institute directors decide the format (online or mixed) depending on where students are, there are eight shelters across the campuses, and subjects such as medicine and dentistry are scheduled near a safe place; a SumDU department page announces an international conference in Sumy on 12 May 2026 (institutional activity, nothing about teaching). overview: Research draft record, unpublished: every statement below is an unverified lead, not a verified fact. A multi-field state university in Sumy, Ukraine, whose Medical Institute (a unit of the university, not a separate university) has taught foreign students; undated official-page leads say Medicine is taught in English and Ukrainian. Draft record built from search-snippet leads on 2026-10-12. Sumy is war-affected and the latest official statement found on teaching format dates from 2022, so whether, where and how foreign students are taught in 2026–27 is an open question. No fee, deadline or intake date is recorded. Every field below is awaiting verification against the official pages listed under research references and nothing here is presented as a current fact.

accreditation.note: Record accreditation only from a NAQA register entry or the official certificate. Nothing recorded. Kept strictly separate: (1) State registration (EDEBO): no register entry surfaced (access limitation, not evidence). (2) Programme licence: no licence document or EDEBO licence record surfaced. (3) National programme accreditation (NAQA): no NAQA decision for Medicine (222) or Dentistry (221) found; NAQA's note on the NAQA–IAAR pilot project says both agencies would reach separate decisions under their own national rules, and SumDU news says the January 26–28, 2022 expert visit had NAQA assess compliance with Ukrainian rules. (4) International accreditation: a university-hosted certificate (search-tool summary) records an accreditation of the Medicine (222) Master's programme by the Independent Agency for Accreditation and Rating (IAAR), Kazakhstan, dated 22 April 2022 and valid through 21 April 2027, also listed in EQAR/DEQAR (THIRD-PARTY European register) as a voluntary programme accreditation; not checked at IAAR, evidenced for the Medicine Master's only (none found for Dentistry or Preventive Medicine), and is NOT NAQA accreditation and NOT recognition. (5) A THIRD-PARTY listing (PhDportal, older) says the State Accreditation Committee gave the university "level IV" accreditation — a legacy institutional status, not a licence or programme accreditation; dated and unverified.

recognition.note: Recognition is decided separately by each destination country's regulator (for example India's National Medical Commission). Record it only from a tier-4 page on a recognition-authority host the owner has listed (N24 b; none listed yet), quoting what that page says, with its date. A World Directory of Medical Schools (WDOMS) listing is a directory entry, not recognition; a university's own claim of WHO, NMC or ECFMG recognition is not recognition; an international accreditation (here IAAR) is not recognition; institutional registration (EDEBO) and programme accreditation (NAQA) are separate claims. Claims seen, none recorded: the university-hosted IAAR certificate says "Recognised by the World Federation of Medical Education (WFME)" (most likely IAAR's own status as an agency; not checked at WFME); an official history page says that in 2009 the Medical Institute "was included to the list of universities database of the World Health Organization" (a directory-listing claim); another result, not identified, claims its graduate programmes are "accredited by the Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates (USA)"; the university says the accreditation "proves that the Institute offers high-quality training of specialists at European standards" (self-description); SumDU news gives the NAQA–IAAR pilot's aim as accrediting programmes "in order to recognize them not only in Ukraine but also abroad" (an aim, not recognition by any regulator); an agency site (THIRD-PARTY) lists "WHO, NMC, ECFMG and FAIMER recognition" — promotional, not evidence. No WDOMS listing was checked and no destination-country regulator statement was found. Never imply a right to practise in any country.
